title: Why Transformers — The Problems with RNNs

questions.question: Why can rnn_style not process all positions in one parallel pass?
options: Each h_t reads the h_{t-1} produced by the previous step
It stores every token in a fixed-size GPU image
It replaces every token with the same arithmetic mean
It requires a separate vocabulary for each position
questions.explanation: The recurrence h = decay*h + x makes the next state depend on the completed previous state, creating a serial dependency.

questions.question: What does depth(4096) return for the RNN and the Hillis–Steele scan?
questions.explanation: depth sets rnn_depth=n and attn_depth=ceil(log2(n)); for 4096 those values are 4096 and 12.

questions.question: What is parallel_scan([1, 2, 3, 4])?
questions.explanation: The scan is a prefix sum, so each output includes all inputs up to that index.

questions.question: What value does attention_style([2.0, 4.0, 6.0]) return?
questions.explanation: This toy attention-style reduction is the order-independent mean: (2+4+6)/3 = 4.

questions.question: What trade-off does the demo state for full attention?
options: It removes serial depth but uses O(N²) memory for an N-token score matrix
It uses O(N) memory but cannot compare two tokens
It keeps O(N) depth and O(N) memory by discarding values
It lowers memory to O(log N) by storing only the final state
questions.explanation: All query-key pairs are represented, so parallel attention has quadratic memory even though its dependency depth is logarithmic in the reduction example.

questions.question: Why should benchmark(n) in this pure-Python file not be read as a GPU speedup measurement?
options: attention_style always sleeps for the GPU kernel launch time
parallel_scan's log-depth graph is still executed by serial Python loops on this CPU
rnn_style uses a different number of input values than attention_style
benchmark measures memory bytes rather than elapsed time
questions.explanation: The code explicitly notes that the Python loop does not expose hardware parallelism; the depth comparison describes the dependency graph, not a GPU execution result.
